correctness.rationale: For all integer m>=3, a nonsingular Vandermonde system yields exact identities giving an ideal E_m^2 isomorphic to the dual numbers. The nonzero square-zero element of the dual numbers rules out a two-dimensional perfect evolution algebra and thus dimension two. An intrinsic residue pencil is nondegenerate for the displayed family and its isomorphism-invariant trace ratio equals a strictly decreasing rational function of m. Every critical identity is derived symbolically and verified by two executable checkers; finite grids are not used for the infinite proof.

value.rationale: Current primary literature explicitly isolates uniqueness of minimal evolution envelopes as an open structural problem. The theorem supplies a strongly nonunique answer for the canonical two-dimensional local algebra: infinitely many isomorphism classes, all minimum possible dimension, with a natural pencil invariant to distinguish them. A single explicit example of dimension three would not answer this finer question, so the family and invariant provide substantive value beyond the known existence/dimension results. No universal classification is claimed.
